chunks: Abu al-Hasan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Hayyah the jurisprudent informed me in what he authorized for me in Balkh, saying: Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Harawi narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Hijr al-Sa'di narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Najih narrated from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family), saying:
Whoever from my nation memorizes forty traditions from the Sunnah, I will be his intercessor on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for memorizing forty hadiths according to this narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* underscores the Shia emphasis on the preservation and transmission of the Sunnah as a means of securing the Prophet’s intercession (shafa'ah) on the Day of Judgment. It reflects the scholarly tradition that even a modest number of well-preserved traditions can serve as a spiritual safeguard, linking the acquisition of religious knowledge directly to eschatological reward.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-16 The jurisprudent Abul Hassan Tahir ibn Muhammad ibn Yunus ibn Hayat - narrated in Balkh that Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Haravy quoted Ja’far ibn Muhammad ibn Sawar, on the authority of Ali ibn Hijr al-Sae’di, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Najih, on the authority of Ata ibn Abi Ribah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “I would intercede on behalf of whoever from my nation who memorizes forty traditions.”
